archetypes.name: integration
archetypes.rationale: Large hard-cutover migration: every missed callsite, allowlist entry, or shell-test stub referencing a retired path will silently break CI; the static reviewers check code quality but not sweep completeness.
archetypes.prompt_body: This diff is a hard-cutover sh-to-Python migration. Your job is to verify that the retired-path sweep is complete across all config and glue files. Check that agent-lint.toml G004 and title-prefix allowlist entries for all deleted .sh, .jq, and .inc.bash paths have been removed and that no stale reference to a retired binary remains as a live allowlist entry. Check that .claude/rules/gh-body-file.md paths list was fully pruned to match only still-live files. Check that scripts/test-legacy-title-prefix-literals-scope.sh ALLOW entries no longer reference retired combine fetch/apply or jq-filter paths. Check that shell test stubs in scripts/test-implement-finalize.sh, skills/implement/scripts/test-refresh-execution-issues.sh, and skills/implement/scripts/test-post-tracking-issue.sh were updated to stub the Python CLI rather than the retired .sh files. Check that Makefile test-harness targets no longer invoke deleted shell harnesses, and that make lint-retired-scripts will pass given the appended python/migrated-scripts.tsv entries. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cli-registration
archetypes.rationale: Twenty-three new CLI verbs must be registered with lazy imports in python/cli.py; a typo or missing entry silently falls through to a confusing AttributeError at runtime, not a loud startup error, so this needs a dedicated pass.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit python/cli.py for completeness and correctness of the new domain/verb registrations added in this diff. Verify that all 23 verbs listed in the plan (release classify-bump, release prepare, release set-version, release finish, release promote, release promote-latest, plugin read-version, verify main, audit-runs preflight, resolve-prs, map-runs, scan-run, compute-counters, title, title-match, pacific-timestamp, close-priors, combine-issues fetch, combine-issues apply, analyze-issues fetch, analyze-issues run, analyze-issues analyze, analyze-issues render-chart) are registered and that each entry uses a lazy import pointing to the correct module and main function name. Check that no new module is imported at the top level of cli.py. Verify that the quiet-mode reinit call before plugin read-version KV emission is present in the correct location relative to the output path, and that it does not unconditionally reinit for other verbs that inherit caller quiet state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
